paper.title: Measure-class classification of achievable Cantorvals
paper.abstract: An achievable Cantorval is a Cantorval that is the set of subsums of a convergent series of positive terms. We construct an explicit achievable Cantorval whose boundary has Lebesgue measure at least $2\prod_{j\ge 1}(1-2^{-j})=0.5775\ldots$. This answers a question of G{\l}{\k{a}}b and Prus-Wi{\'s}niowski and gives a counterexample to the conjecture of Nowakowski and Prus-Wi{\'s}niowski that every achievable Cantorval is standard. The example is generated by a hybrid series of Pratsiovytyi, Vynnyshyn and Vynnyshyn. The lower bound comes from an isolated-digit criterion, which produces a Cantor subset of the boundary whose measure is an explicit infinite product; after rescaling, the boundary measure can be made arbitrarily close to $1$. We also prove that the boundary of every achievement set is either Lebesgue null or has positive measure near each of its points. Consequently, up to homeomorphisms that preserve Lebesgue null sets in both directions, there are exactly two achievable Cantorvals, distinguished by whether the boundary is null. For boundaries of positive measure, the homeomorphism can be chosen so that it changes the normalized boundary measure of every Borel set by a factor arbitrarily close to $1$. For general Cantorvals we classify the case of a relatively clopen boundary support and show that further invariants appear beyond this case. Finally, the null-set preserving self-homeomorphisms of a Cantorval always form a meager subgroup of its homeomorphism group. This subgroup is dense exactly when the support of Lebesgue measure on the boundary is empty or the whole boundary; in particular, it is dense for every achievable Cantorval.

paper.title: Sharp $s$-nice recurrence without the van der Corput property
paper.abstract: For every real $s>2$, we construct a set $R_s\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ which is a set of $t$-nice measurable recurrence exactly for $t\ge s$ and is not a van der Corput set. The new ingredient of this construction is the Density Frankl--R\"odl theorem. Furthermore, the probability measure $\sigma_s$ which witnesses failure of the van der Corput property has an atom at zero with mass $(s-2)/(2s-2)$. A Gaussian tail argument proves both sharpness of the recurrence exponent and the fact that this atom is the largest possible for any $s$-nice recurrent set. The result sharpens the recurrence separations of Bourgain and Mountakis, answers a question of Mountakis about the maximal mass of an atom at zero, and answers a question of Forrest about separating the various degrees of nice recurrence. In the appendix we give a self-contained proof of the Density Frankl-R\"odl theorem.

paper.title: KAM theory for contact Hamiltonian systems
paper.abstract: In both finite and infinite dimensions, we establish the first frequency-preserving KAM theorems for full-dimensional Legendrian tori in contact Hamiltonian families with general analytic coupling between the momenta and the contact variable. After adjustment of external parameters, the flow on each torus is analytically conjugate in the original time to the prescribed translation, with estimates uniform as the damping parameter crosses zero. This coupling can generate nonzero mean damping at first order even when the damping parameter vanishes. In finite dimensions, nonzero mean damping yields a time-preserving analytic contact linearization near the torus. In both settings the invariant graphs give global analytic solutions of stationary Hamilton--Jacobi equations whose characteristic flows are conjugate to the prescribed translation. A novel consequence in finite dimensions is that, under global Tonelli assumptions and strict increase in the contact variable, this analytic solution is both the unique forward and the unique backward weak KAM solution, and its associated Legendrian graph is an invariant torus carrying quasi-periodic dynamics.

paper.title: Eight limit cycles in a three-dimensional competitive Lotka-Volterra system
paper.abstract: Gyllenberg and Yan conjectured that a three-dimensional competitive Lotka-Volterra system can have at least five limit cycles. We prove the conjecture by constructing a strictly competitive system in which eight distinct limit cycles coexist near a single positive equilibrium. For each $m=5,6,7,8$, we construct a weak focus of order $m$ and identify parameter directions on the Hopf hypersurface that allow us to vary the first $m-1$ focus quantities independently. We choose these quantities so that the drift of a scalar amplitude function alternates in sign on $m$ nested level curves, forcing a limit cycle between each consecutive pair. A perturbation transverse to the Hopf hypersurface creates one additional cycle inside the others. The one-turn displacement map shows that both local counts are sharp. For each $m$, we give a rigorous computer-assisted proof that an explicit rational interaction matrix yields at least $m$ distinct hyperbolic limit cycles. They proved this conjecture for non-degenerate star-shaped hypersurfaces in ${\bf R}^6$. Motivated by their work, we study the symmetric counterpart of this problem. We prove that if a symmetric compact star-shaped hypersurface $\Sigma$ in ${\bf R}^4$ carries only finitely many geometrically distinct prime symmetric closed characteristics, and every odd iterate of them is non-degenerate in the symmetric sense, then each of them has nonzero symmetric mean index. Based on this result, we further prove that if $\Sigma$ carries exactly two geometrically distinct prime symmetric closed characteristics and all their iterates are non-degenerate, then both of them are irrationally elliptic.

paper.title: High order tangencies, paratangencies, and universal dynamics
paper.abstract: Our research focuses on studying the dynamics in the Newhouse domain $\mathcal N(L)$ -- open regions in the space of $C^r$ diffeomorphisms of a $d$-dimensional manifold $\mathcal M^d$ ($r=1,\ldots,\infty,\omega$ and $d\ge 2$) where homoclinic tangencies to a saddle periodic orbit $L$ are persistent. If $L$ is a bi-focus, we reveal novel bifurcations in $\mathcal N(L)$ showing density of diffeomorphisms with infinitely many corank-2 homoclinic tangencies of all orders. These results entail genericity of one- or two-dimensional universal dynamics in $\mathcal N(L)$ (depending on the type of $L$). Moreover, we characterize the geometric complexity of the bifurcation sets corresponding to homoclinic tangencies. We prove that parametric families with paratangencies of arbitrarily high orders are dense in the space of parametric families intersecting $\mathcal N(L)$. If $r\le\infty$ and $L$ is sectionally dissipative, this implies density of families possessing infinitely many coexisting stable periodic orbits for some open set of parameter values.

paper.title: Fast growth of periodic orbits, translated points and short Floer bars for contactomorphisms
paper.abstract: We establish arbitrarily fast growth of distinct periodic orbits and geometrically distinct translated points for contactomorphisms of the unit cotangent bundle of a closed hyperbolic surface. For a specified analytically admissible normalized Rabinowitz Floer family on a closed contact manifold with Liouville filling, we bound fixed-window barcode entropy by topological entropy. The proof compares long-bar counts with graph volume through contact tomography and filtered continuation. Under strong translated nondegeneracy, we show that super-exponential translated-pair growth in a compact interior window forces super-exponential growth of short bars born in the surrounding window.

paper.title: Analytical modelling of compliance dynamics under fiscal feedback: tipping thresholds, intervention costs and hysteresis
paper.abstract: Compliance with taxes and other collective obligations is often enforced with resources that come from those who comply, so that non-compliance erodes its own deterrent. We develop an exactly solvable dynamical model of compliance under this fiscal feedback. Individuals choose between paying and evading by imitating those who do better, and the budget against evasion is a share of the revenue, split between enforcement and education. The model yields closed-form expressions for the equilibria, the tipping thresholds and their bifurcations, the budgets needed to maintain compliance and to restore it after a collapse, and the recovery time near the threshold. Fiscal feedback alone does not produce tipping points: hysteresis appears only when an instrument that changes individual incentives, such as fines or education, is funded by the tax base. Stronger sanctions reduce both the maintenance and the rescue budget, but beyond a critical level they make the system bistable, so that the choice of sanction is a trade-off between efficiency and resilience, which we quantify with a resilience indicator and a resilience-constrained design problem. The cheapest allocation of the budget between enforcement and education is also obtained in closed form. A sensitivity analysis identifies the parameters that control prevention and recovery costs, and stochastic simulations of individual agents and a slow budget cycle confirm the analytical predictions. The framework provides quantitative guidelines for allocating scarce intervention resources in tax compliance and in other enforcement problems with similar feedbacks.

paper.title: On the linear stability of elliptic relative equilibrium in planar restricted $(n+1)$-body problem
paper.abstract: In this paper, we consider the restricted $(n+1)$-body problems, where the $n$ primaries forming an a homographic motion generated by the planar central configuration, and the massless particle is attracted by this $n$ primaries. We are interested in the linear stability of the elliptic relative equilibria of the massless particle under the pulsating coordinates. The main contribution of this paper first lies in the investigation of a general $(\alpha,\beta)$-system (1.7). We obtain large-range spectral instability and small-range stability results valid for arbitrary eccentricity. The restricted $(n+1)$-body problem arises as a special case of this system. Accordingly, we derive several criteria for spectral instability and linear stability for this problem. As a final application, we establish some stability results of elliptic relative equilibria for massless particle under some special central configurations.

paper.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the higher order differentiability of physical measures, in the category of smooth expanding endomorphisms of compact manifolds, and we establish the explicit response formulae of any order. Furthermore, we provide the solutions to the high order request problem, which is regarded as the inverse problem to response formulae, that is, we make perturbations to realize prescribed responses up to any finite order, and we establish the existence of minimizers for a relaxed optimization problem associated with suitable cost functionals.

paper.title: Levi Dynamics and Largest Domains of Discontinuity on Flag Manifolds
paper.abstract: Divergent sequences in a semisimple Lie group have a bounded Levi part that is invisible to Cartan projections and limit flags. We show that this Levi part is a genuine dynamical invariant and determines much of the large-scale behaviour of discrete groups on flag manifolds. For every real flag manifold, we compute the complete moving-source destination relation of a divergent sequence, including the Levi contribution. This yields a stratified convergence principle, a boundary compactification encoding the relation, and an exact properness criterion. For discrete groups the relation organises the classical limit sets into a single flag, from Quint's limit set through the recurrent and Kulkarni sets to the Myrberg set, the complement of equicontinuity. Sequences with coalescing limit flags satisfy a diagonal formula, which gives a recurrence criterion for the largest domain of proper discontinuity. For compact twists of Kleinian groups, the criterion becomes an exact incidence condition on the twist closure on every Grassmannian and Lagrangian Grassmannian. Two strongly irreducible subgroups of $\mathrm{PGL}(8,\mathbb{C})$ with identical marked Cartan projections, limit flags and destination relations on $\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^7$ are distinguished on $\operatorname{Gr}(4,\mathbb{C}^8)$ alone. We also show that marked boundary data recover the compact twist while unmarked data recover only its orbit partition. Further applications treat critical projective dynamics, cusped Hitchin groups and symmetric powers.

paper.title: From Low-Dimensional Chaos to High-Dimensional Dynamics in Self-Attention Systems
paper.abstract: Continuous-time particle models of self-attention are often studied under symmetry assumptions that yield a gradient structure and constrain the dynamics to convergence toward equilibria. We investigate the behavior of these systems beyond the gradient setting, considering autonomous projected self-attention models with constant query, key, and value matrices and particles constrained to an ellipse. For three particles, the equations define a vector field on the three-dimensional torus. We derive explicit synchronized periodic solutions and compute their Floquet multipliers, establishing the existence of non-gradient dynamics. Numerical explorations using bifurcation diagrams, Poincare sections, periodic-orbit continuation, a nd Lyapunov exponents reveal attracting periodic orbits, invariant-torus-like behavior, and strong evidence of chaos. We then construct higher-dimensional systems by coupling these low-dimensional building blocks through masked and multi-head attention mechanisms. We discuss the persistence of normally hyperbolic invariant manifolds under weak coupling and investigate how the coupling architecture influences the resulting dynamics. Numerical experiments reveal the emergence of additional expanding directions, including a 60-particle system in which 26 of the 40 computed Lyapunov exponents exceed 0.01. These results demonstrate the richness of the dynamical behavior possible in simplified self-attention systems and motivate further investigation of the invariant structures organizing their high-dimensional dynamics.

paper.title: Computable certificates for data-driven dimension reduction on reaction-diffusion lattices
paper.abstract: Data-driven methods recover low-dimensional coordinates from high-dimensional spatiotemporal data. Whether those coordinates track a genuine invariant object or a finite-resolution artifact is not settled. On reaction-diffusion lattices, the spectral-gap condition of inertial-manifold theory reduces to a critical lattice size $n_*$. Below $n_*$, the two-dimensional diffusion-map reading carries an existence guarantee; above $n_*$ the guarantee lapses, and this lapse does not rule out a slow manifold. The closed form for $n_*$ follows from the reaction Lipschitz constant and the slow-mode growth rate. The certificate is tested on a quadratic and a cubic model system. At the Brusselator boundary the existence sign is checked by interval enclosure, and the spectral margin decays as $n^{-4}$ across the transition. On strongly damped Hopf lattices the slow manifold collapses to the uniform limit cycle; this degeneracy, the trivial graph $\varphi\equiv0$, is reported directly rather than concealed. The boundary gives a PDE-side prior for data-driven reduction: it marks the resolution at which a recovered two-dimensional structure can be trusted.

For strongly damped Hopf lattices the slow manifold degenerates to the uniform cycle with trivial graph. The explicit threshold and full hypotheses: Not specified in the abstract.

paper.title: Synchronisation under quasi-periodic forcing of circle diffeomorphisms with two attracting and two repelling fixed points
paper.abstract: We study the dynamics of circle diffeomorphisms, which have exactly two attracting and two repelling fixed points, under quasi-periodic forcing. For sufficiently small forcing, such a system exhibits uniformly hyperbolic behaviour. The results focus on systems with larger forcing, where every orbit intersects the basins of attraction of both attracting fixed points infinitely often. For such quasi-periodically forced circle diffeomorphisms, we identify a set of parameters of positive measure for which the corresponding skew-product systems admit a unique attracting and a unique repelling invariant graph, which capture the dynamics of Lebesgue almost every point on $\mathbb{T}^2$. Further, we show that both continuous invariant graphs and invariant graphs that are discontinuous on a dense set can occur within the same class of forced circle diffeomorphisms, for different quasi-periodic rotations on the base.

In the larger-forcing regime where each orbit visits both attracting basins infinitely often, a positive-measure parameter set has a unique attracting and unique repelling invariant graph describing Lebesgue almost every point of \(\mathbb T^2\). Different quasi-periodic base rotations in the same class can yield continuous graphs or graphs discontinuous on a dense set. paper.title: Sierpi\'{n}ski Gaskets Julia set and Postcritically finite fractals
paper.abstract: Devaney's work on the Julia sets of the McMullen family, established these rational maps as central objects in holomorphic dynamics. For Misiurewicz parameters, that is when the orbits of the critical points are all strictly preperiodic to a repelling cycle, the topological point of view taken by Kameyama links the dynamics of such rational maps to that on the attractors of invertible self-similar iterated function system. Ero\u{g}lu, Rohde, and Solomyak showed that in favorable cases the topological conjugacy is in fact quasisymmetric. We survey the machinery underlying these results and propose directions for further research.

paper.title: Periodic orbit asymptotics and dynamical zeta functions for smooth surface diffeomorphisms
paper.abstract: Let $f$ be a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of a closed surface $M$, and let $H$ be a closed homoclinic class with topological entropy $h=h_{\mathrm{top}}(f|H)>0$ and homoclinic period $\ell$. We prove that \[ \forall\,0<\chi<h,\qquad \lim_{\ell\mid n,\;n\to\infty} \frac{\#\mathrm{Per}_\chi(n,H)}{e^{nh}}=\ell, \] where $\mathrm{Per}_\chi(n,H)$ denotes the saddle points in $H$ of least period $n$ whose Lyapunov exponents lie outside $[-\chi,\chi]$. We also prove exponential remainders for the class and global counting formulas. As a result, for every $0<\chi<h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$, the Artin--Mazur zeta function of all $\chi$-hyperbolic periodic orbits, including sinks and sources, extends meromorphically beyond its disk of convergence. Its leading poles are determined by the periods of the ergodic maximal measures. This answers the meromorphic continuation question of Buzzi.

analysis.relevance_note: Entropy-controlled periodic counting and zeta functions directly match entropy and orbit-complexity interests.
analysis.tldr: Hyperbolic least-period saddle counts in a closed homoclinic class have an entropy asymptotic with period factor, and the hyperbolic zeta function extends meromorphically.
analysis.problem: Obtain periodic-orbit asymptotics and zeta continuation for smooth surface diffeomorphisms.
analysis.main_result: Let \(f\) be a \(C^\infty\) diffeomorphism of a closed surface and \(H\) a closed homoclinic class with entropy \(h>0\) and homoclinic period \(\ell\). For each \(0<\chi<h\), the number of least-period-\(n\) saddles in \(H\) with exponents outside \([-\chi,\chi]\), divided by \(e^{nh}\), tends to \(\ell\) along multiples of \(\ell\). The authors also give exponential remainders and global formulas. For every \(0<\chi<h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)\), the Artin-Mazur zeta function of all \(\chi\)-hyperbolic orbits, including sinks and sources, extends meromorphically beyond its convergence disk; leading poles are determined by periods of ergodic maximal measures. paper.title: Degree 2 foliations on $\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ with only saddle-node and nilpotent singularities
paper.abstract: We classify all foliations of degree $2$ on $\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ having only saddle-node or nilpotent singularities up to projective equivalence. To do so, we use the bijection between such foliations and their polar configurations stated by Campillo and Olivares~\cite{CO}. We also show that three families of the found foliations admit no algebraic invariant curve.

paper.title: Algorithms and topological invariants for dynamic systems. IV. Topological Equivalence of Functions and Hamiltonian Dynamical Systems
paper.abstract: This is the fourth part of a series on algorithms and topological invariants for dynamical systems. We study the topological equivalence of smooth functions and of Hamiltonian flows on surfaces, and the discrete invariants, Reeb graphs and cell decompositions, that classify them. We recall the notions of topological equivalence and structural stability, introduce two equivalences of functions (with and without the order of the critical values) and show that simple Morse functions on closed orientable surfaces are classified by their Reeb graphs with vertex odering, while simple Hamiltonian flows are classified by Reeb graphs with marked edges. For the disc and for the sphere we obtain a recursive description and a generating function for the numbers of such trees, and compute the numbers of topologically non-equivalent simple Morse functions and Hamiltonian flows with a given number of saddles. We also describe functions with isolated, possibly degenerate, critical points by cell decompositions, and give an algorithm and computational results for functions with three critical points. In the first part (arXiv:2501.15657) we discussed the basic concepts of differential topology. In the second part (arXiv:2502.00506) we discussed the discrete topological structures used in the topological theory of dynamical systems. In the third part (arXiv:2502.09958) we constructed algorithms that recognize $2$- and $3$-manifolds in simplicial complexes and regular CW-complexes and determine the topological type of a $2$-manifold (connectivity, orientability, genus, number of boundary components).

The author distinguishes function equivalence with and without critical-value order. Recursive tree descriptions and generating functions count disc and sphere examples by saddle number. Cell decompositions describe isolated possibly degenerate critical points, with algorithms and computations for three-critical-point functions. paper.title: Bifurcation Structure and Coexisting Dynamical States in Two Inductively Coupled Josephson Junctions
paper.abstract: Inductively coupled Josephson junctions support coexisting stationary and running states whose selection depends on both circuit parameters and initial conditions. We investigate the model of a direct current-driven resistively and capacitively shunted junction pair as coupled nonlinear oscillators at zero external magnetic flux, allowing unequal bias, damping and inductive coupling parameters. Equilibrium equations, nullclines, and Jacobian spectra are combined with multiple-initial-condition simulations, finite-time Lyapunov spectra, and Poincar\'e returns to characterize changes in the system dynamics under varying initial conditions and parameter settings. The fixed-point bifurcation diagrams reveal the creation, destruction or annihilation of equilibria and non-monotonic changes in their number under asymmetric coupling. In representative asymmetric parameter slices, nondegenerate saddle-node bifurcations generate or terminate stable equilibria within intervals that also support periodic or chaotic running motion. The running dynamics exhibit period-doubling, period-cascading sequences and embedded periodic windows within chaotic regions, while the initial-condition scans resolve their coexistence with stationary states. These results connect the local equilibrium structure with the parameter-dependent organization and selection of dynamical regimes in the coupled-junction system.

paper.title: Automorphism groups of mixing shifts of finite type
paper.abstract: We prove that nontrivial two-sided mixing shifts of finite type are flip conjugate if and only if their automorphism groups are abstractly commensurable. This resolves an outstanding question of Boyle, Lind, and Rudolph from 1988.

paper.title: A mean index criterion for multiple closed characteristics
paper.abstract: Let $n\ge2$. We prove that a compact strictly star-shaped $C^3$ hypersurface in $\mathbb R^{2n}$ carries at least $n$ geometrically distinct prime closed characteristics if all iterates are nondegenerate and all mean indices are at least one. It suffices that all mean indices are positive and that the bound holds only for prime characteristics with negative mean Euler characteristic in the variational grading. The proof uses a minimum argument for the global Morse remainder and requires no individual index exclusion. For odd $n\ge3$, we obtain a smaller, dimension-dependent strict bound when good iterates of Maslov-type index $-1$ are excluded. Irrational ellipsoids show that the multiplicity bound is sharp.

paper.title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems II: Upper Right Quadrant
paper.abstract: We study finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in the upper right quadrant. For two vortices with arbitrary nonzero circulations and distinct initial positions, we prove global existence and uniqueness by excluding interior collisions, boundary approach, and finite-time escape to infinity. For three vortices with arbitrary nonzero circulations, we rule out finite-time boundary approach in the limit inferior sense, without assuming boundedness or convergence of the trajectories. The argument combines Hamiltonian estimates, monotonicity of signed coordinate moments, and geometric estimates adapted to both walls and the corner. We also establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse for every nonzero circulation triple whose pairwise products sum to zero. The collapse point can be prescribed arbitrarily in the interior, with any sufficiently small positive collapse time. The resulting solutions are asymptotically self-similar, exhibiting square-root contraction and logarithmic rotation. They are constructed using a local strong stable manifold of real dimension two in a similarity system augmented by a complex scale.

paper.title: Rollout Scheduling for Chaotic Neural ODEs: Coverage Gains, Computational Cost, and Predictive Accuracy
paper.abstract: Training Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Neural ODEs) on chaotic systems is difficult because small changes in model parameters can lead to rapidly growing differences in predictions. A rollout is a trajectory predicted by the model. Choosing its length from a single global Lyapunov time overlooks differences in local instability. We study rollout scheduling for training on one contiguous rollout per sampled state, asking whether adapting its length to local instability improves prediction. We find the schedule that uses the most trajectory data under an instability budget, a limit on how much instability any one rollout may accumulate. Under stated assumptions, we bound the resulting coverage gain and the coverage lost when the instability estimates are in error. Numerical checks illustrate the theory. Training experiments on Lorenz-63, Lorenz-96, and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky compare adaptive and constant schedules at the same instability budgets and maximum rollout lengths. The budgets are computed from the true system's finite-time Lyapunov exponents. Across the tested settings, adaptive schedules increase trajectory coverage at additional computational cost, without showing a consistent improvement in prediction accuracy. On Lorenz-63, limiting adaptive rollouts to the horizon used to estimate instability improves prediction at the larger budgets. On Kuramoto--Sivashinsky, most configurations provide useful short-time predictions, while all tested long rollouts eventually fail. These findings show why coverage, prediction accuracy, and long-time behavior need separate evaluation, and why instability estimates should be checked over the windows used in training.

paper.title: The Thue-Morse route to chaos in the open quantum baker map
paper.abstract: We study the resonances of the quantum baker map opened by a window of width $w$ centred at $q_c$. For $q_c=1/2$ the survivor set of the classical doubling map with a hole goes from zero to positive topological entropy along the Thue-Morse route, and we find numerically, for $N$ up to $2^{25}$, that the resonance spectrum follows this route step by step, also where the entropy is zero. Below the threshold $w_c=4a^*-1$, with $a^*$ the Thue-Morse constant, the surviving cycles have periods $2^\nu$ and their thresholds accumulate doubly exponentially. Each cycle gives, as isolated orbits do, a multiplet of resonances close to modulus $2^{-1/2}$, with phases set by its action. Since a cycle is resolved only if its period is shorter than about $\log_2 N$, twice the Ehrenfest time, about $\log_2\log_2 N$ steps are resolved, four at our largest sizes. Near $w_c$ the 16-cycle perturbs the 8-multiplet through a return path that classically opens only at $w_c$. Cutting a few sites of this path removes the perturbation. At $w_c$ the leading resonance jumps within one or two lattice sites, since a window one site wider than the threshold already has an entropy of order $1/\log_2 N$. One site or more above $w_c$ it lies between 0.93 and 1.00 times the value set by the topological pressure, with no free parameter. There the Walsh eigenvalue count grows with the fractal Weyl exponent, and the Fourier count with an exponent a few hundredths smaller at the sizes we reach.

analysis.tldr: Numerical quantum-baker resonances follow the classical Thue-Morse entropy route, with finite-resolution thresholds and pressure-based resonance scaling.

The threshold is \(w_c=4a^*-1\). Surviving period-\(2^\nu\) cycles yield multiplets near modulus \(2^{-1/2}\), resolved only when their period is below about \(\log_2N\). paper.title: Nonlinear Moments as Equivalence Classes: A Lyapunov-Perron Approach to the Invariance Equation

paper.abstract: The linear moment is well defined whenever the system and the exosystem have disjoint spectra. Its nonlinear counterpart is not: the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the invariance equation that defines it are in general not guaranteed, so additional assumptions such as Poisson stability of the exosystem and the exponential stability of the system are required to define the nonlinear moment. This paper reduces this asymmetry. By using the Lyapunov--Perron fixed-point argument, we show that under a condition called the strip condition, there exist local $\mathcal C^N$ solutions, with $N$ determined by the system and the exosystem, and every pair of $\mathcal C^1$ solutions has contact of order $k^-$, where $k$ is a spectral ratio determined by the system and the exosystem; the solutions are flat-equivalent when $k=\infty$. Based on this observation, we extend the concept of nonlinear moment as an equivalence class of functions rather than a function. The polynomial of degree $N$ or formal power series ansatz of the invariance equation are the distinguished representatives of the equivalence class. We also show that, when the system is exponentially stable, the moment describes the output shared by all trajectories up to the order $k^-$, which gives the moment a time-domain interpretation when the steady-state interpretation is not available. Finally, we show that the concept of moment matching also naturally extends as the definition of nonlinear moment is extended to an equivalence class. The ansatz also plays a crucial role in the extended notion of moment matching. The results are illustrated by a numerical example.

analysis.tldr: Under a strip condition, nonlinear moments become equivalence classes of invariance-equation solutions with controlled order of contact.

Any two \(\mathcal C^1\) solutions have contact of order \(k^-\), where \(k\) is their spectral ratio; for \(k=\infty\) they are flat-equivalent. Degree-\(N\) polynomial or formal-series ansätze give distinguished representatives of the nonlinear-moment class. With exponential system stability, all trajectory outputs agree with the moment up to order \(k^-\). Moment matching is extended accordingly, with a numerical example. paper.title: Vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and boundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type
paper.abstract: In present paper, for functional-differential equations of retarded type, the method of vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and the method of higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals are developed. On the basis of this methods, sufficient conditions for various types of uniform boundedness of solutions and sufficient conditions for various types of ultimate-uniform boundedness of solutions are obtained.

paper.title: The Z[tau]-foam: Goodman-Strauss's Dodecafoam as arithmetic in the icosahedral module
paper.abstract: Goodman-Strauss's Dodecafoam is a substitution that fills the regular dodecahedron with dodecahedral bubbles of sizes tau^{-k}, tau=(1+sqrt(5))/2, using the seven kinds of cells into which the twelve planes of its stellation cut it. We rewrite it as exact arithmetic in one Z[tau]-module of rank three, the span M of the six five-fold axes, on which the icosahedral group acts by 120 matrices in GL(3,Z[tau]). A placed inflated copy of a cell is a union of cells iff its facet levels lie in {+-1,+-tau^3} and it lies in the dodecahedron. Solving this finite linear system for all scales at once gives exactly the 22 rules known from a geometric search; no rule exists at any scale other than 1,tau,tau^2,tau^3. The substitution becomes integer arithmetic on six-tuples and reproduces the bubbles of the geometric foam exactly. Whether a point of M is the centre of a bubble of size tau^{-k} is decided by at most k+3 exact sign vectors (its address), without building the foam, and all bubbles of one size are obtained by sieving the points of M whose Galois conjugate satisfies |x^*|<=2 tau^k, a bound we prove with computer assistance. The number of bubbles of size tau^{-k} is A beta^k+O(|beta'|^k) with beta=(1+sqrt(29))/2. Hence the closure of the rescaled conjugates of the bubble centres has box dimension at most log_tau(beta)=2.4123<3, and the bubbles are not selected by any cut-and-project window with interior. The other foams of the 1999 article are sub-foams of this one. The 50400 substitutions allowed by the rule list give 18899 bubble sets, and the Dodecafoam is a product set of 13440 of them, to the depth tested. In four dimensions the same linear system, for the star cut of the 120-cell, reproduces the 718 clusters of a geometric search and adds the scale sqrt(5) tau^2.

paper.title: On rescuing diverging algorithms: crossing infinity in continuous Newton methods via a self-similarity detection framework
paper.abstract: We address the solution of systems of nonlinear algebraic equations via continuous Newton methods; these methods reformulate the discrete Newton update as an initial value problem for a system of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) whose stationary points correspond to the desired roots. A fundamental challenge arises when the Jacobian of these ODEs becomes singular along the solution trajectory, inducing blow-up in the vector field --or in the state itself-- and causing the numerical integration to break down before reaching the desired root. To overcome this difficulty, we propose a directional self-similar blow-up detection and crossing procedure, wrapped around an adaptive step-size ODE solver with event detection. The method assumes local self-similar behavior near the blow-up; the self-similarity exponent, blow-up time, and amplitude are estimated on the fly from a short sequence of threshold crossings via linear regression, requiring no prior knowledge of the singularity location, its order, or the blow-up regime---in contrast to approaches that rely on explicit analytical continuation or problem-specific coordinate transformations. The estimated exponent distinguishes two qualitatively different scenarios at finite time: one in which only the vector field diverges while the state remains finite, admitting an explicit integral correction, and one in which the state itself blows-up. In addition, infinite-time divergence of the state (the so-called "grow-up" regime) is handled through a suitable time reparameterization. In higher dimensions, we track the norm of the vector field along its instantaneous direction; near a simple singularity, the flow asymptotically aligns with a single dominant direction (see text), reducing detection and estimation to a scalar problem regardless of ambient space dimension.

paper.title: Contact rigidity and Poisson bracket invariants
paper.abstract: We study $C^0$-rigidity and Poisson bracket invariants on closed contact manifolds. We prove that Poisson commutation is closed under uniform convergence, establish weak rigidity for pairs without common zeros, and obtain lower semicontinuity under quantitative control of Reeb derivatives. A three-dimensional counterexample shows that unrestricted weak rigidity fails. For partitions of unity, the contact bracket itself controls the Reeb derivatives. Using monotone homogeneous quasi-morphisms and the Cant--Kilgore--Zhang spectral invariant, we derive positive lower bounds for invariants of open covers and configurations of compact subsets. Applications include a quantitative contact big fiber theorem, bounds on Hamiltonian chord durations and Reeb travel times, and deformations of contact one-forms.

paper.title: Infinitely many spectral gaps for Anderson--Bernoulli operators with sparse periodic backgrounds
paper.abstract: We consider discrete Anderson--Bernoulli operators with a periodic background. At a single coupling, every minimal period of at least three admits a background with at most four nonzero sites per period whose almost sure spectrum has infinitely many gaps. We give two constructions. The first uses at most seven nonzero sites per period and fixes the accumulation point at zero. For periods of at least five, the second uses exactly four nonzero sites per period and takes the lowest Dirichlet eigenvalue of the inserted chain as the accumulation point. In both constructions the gaps approach from the right. The widths of the selected gaps and their distances to the accumulation point are comparable to a common geometric factor divided by the period in the first family and by its cube in the second. Spectral intervals of comparable length separate successive gaps in each selected sequence.

paper.title: Principal Eigenvalues for Transport-Nonlocal Operators on Compact Manifolds: Ergodic Averages and Quotient Reduction
paper.abstract: We study principal eigenvalues for transport--nonlocal operators on connected compact Riemannian manifolds. Transport changes the natural spectral threshold from the pointwise maximum of the potential to a maximal invariant average. We establish a necessary and sufficient criterion based on a resolvent spectral radius and derive sufficient existence conditions for uniquely ergodic flows and, through quotient reduction, for flows arising from compact abelian Lie group actions. Examples on the two-dimensional torus show that, for weak nonlocal coupling, transport can create or suppress principal eigenvalues, while sphere rotations illustrate how the quotient criterion accommodates singular orbits.

paper.title: Regularity of invariant measures of solutions for fractional stochastic partial differential equations with memory and nonlinear noise
paper.abstract: We are concerned with stochastic fractional partial differential equations involving memory and nonlinear multiplicative noise. Based on the well-known Dafermos method, a suitable variable defined by the integrated past history is introduced. This transformation not only overcomes the non-Markovianity of the original problem which prevents us from analyzing invariant measures for the associated Markov semigroup, but also facilitates the analysis of the well-posedness together with the Faedo-Galerkin approximations and Minty's technique. Moreover, we prove the existence of invariant measures by the classical Krylov-Bogoliubov approach, and further establish the regularity of invariant measures by virtue of a control argument.

analysis.relevance_note: Invariant measures and Markov-semigroup recovery give a direct random-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: A history-variable reformulation yields invariant measures and their regularity for the stated fractional stochastic equations.
analysis.problem: Overcome memory-induced non-Markovianity and study invariant-measure regularity.
analysis.main_result: For fractional stochastic PDEs with memory and nonlinear multiplicative noise, an integrated-history variable restores a setting suitable for Markov-semigroup analysis. The authors establish well-posedness, existence of invariant measures and regularity of those measures. The transformation uses the Dafermos method; well-posedness combines Faedo-Galerkin approximations and Minty technique, existence uses Krylov-Bogoliubov, and regularity uses a control argument. The precise equation assumptions and regularity spaces: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Stochastic evolution with memory and invariant probability measures.

paper.title: Certified $p$-adic normal forms: an Eliasson-Vey theorem and zero sets of orbits
paper.abstract: I use the Smith form of the homological operator to construct partial Poincar\'e-Dulac normal forms near an equilibrium of a vector field on $\mathbb {Z}_p^d$ with coefficients divisible by $p$ (by $4$ if $p=2$). Retaining the directions whose removal would cost more than a fixed number of digits gives convergence on an explicit ball for any linear part. For polynomial fields, an exact integer check of the conjugacy defect certifies the computed flow to $K$ digits in rescaled coordinates. When the quadratic parts of an integrable Hamiltonian system at a rank-$0$ point span a Cartan subalgebra, the homological divisors in symplectic eigencoordinates are integers. This lets me use Newton iteration to obtain an exact $p$-adic Eliasson--Vey normal form at every prime and for every Williamson type. In exact linear normal coordinates, a polynomial restricted to an orbit gives a sum of exponentials, to which van der Poorten's bound of $2s-3$ zeros applies for a nonzero sum with $s\ge2$ distinct exponents. For integer orbits of polynomial maps, I combine exact modular orbits, Strassmann bounds and archimedean estimates in an adelic sieve. At every prime, increasing the modular depth eventually excludes a time class exactly when the interpolation along its center-manifold shadow has no zero in $\mathbb {Z}_p$.

analysis.relevance_note: Local conjugacy, integrable normal forms and orbit zero sets give a related arithmetic-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: Certified partial p-adic normal forms and an integrable exact normal form yield orbit-zero bounds and an adelic exclusion criterion.
analysis.problem: Compute and certify p-adic normal forms and use them to study zeros along orbits.
analysis.main_result: For fields on \(\mathbb Z_p^d\) with coefficients divisible by \(p\), or by four at \(p=2\), Smith form of the homological operator yields convergent partial Poincaré-Dulac normal forms on explicit balls for any linear part. Polynomial conjugacy-defect checks certify a rescaled flow to \(K\) digits. If integrable Hamiltonian quadratic parts at rank zero span a Cartan subalgebra, integer homological divisors permit Newton iteration to an exact Eliasson-Vey form at every prime and Williamson type. In exact linear coordinates, a nonzero exponential sum with \(s\geq2\) exponents has at most \(2s-3\) zeros. A modular/Strassmann/archimedean sieve eventually excludes a time class exactly when the center-manifold-shadow interpolation has no p-adic zero.
analysis.context: p-adic local dynamics, Hamiltonian normal forms and arithmetic orbit intersections.

paper.title: Exceptional Rays of Invariant Processes on Trees
paper.abstract: Let $A$ be an ergodic, non-constant random process on the $d$-regular tree $T_d$, with marginal distribution $X$. We prove that there always exist "exceptional" rays, whose asymptotic means are at least $\mathbb{E}(X)+\delta$; furthermore, for edge processes, $\delta > 0$ can be taken to depend only on the law of $X$. We compare different definitions of "maximal asymptotic means", relating them to different notions of speed of tree-indexed random walks.

analysis.relevance_note: Ergodicity and asymptotic orbit-like averages on invariant tree processes give a related probabilistic-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: Every stated nonconstant ergodic tree process has rays with asymptotic mean strictly above the marginal expectation.
analysis.problem: Find exceptional rays and compare maximal asymptotic means for invariant processes on regular trees.
analysis.main_result: For an ergodic nonconstant random process on the \(d\)-regular tree with marginal \(X\), exceptional rays have asymptotic means at least \(\mathbb E(X)+\delta\) for positive \(\delta\). For edge processes, \(\delta\) depends only on the law of \(X\). The authors compare definitions of maximal asymptotic mean through speeds of tree-indexed random walks. Integrability assumptions, quantitative values and proof techniques: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Invariant random tree processes, ergodicity and exceptional averages.

paper.title: Trajectory arclength reveals thermodynamic criticality
paper.abstract: Thermodynamic criticality arises at continuous phase transitions, where collective interactions produce non-analytic behavior in equilibrium thermodynamic quantities in the thermodynamic limit. We show that this criticality also leaves an analytically predictable signature in the arclength of microscopic Hamiltonian trajectories. For the attractive Hamiltonian mean-field model, we derive the thermodynamic limit of the equilibrium-averaged arclength, formulated as a normalized Lagrangian descriptor, and demonstrate that it develops a kink precisely at the phase transition. We trace this non-analyticity to spontaneous magnetization and derive the leading critical finite-size correction, scaling as $N^{-1/2}$ with an explicit analytical prefactor. Simulations with up to $10^5$ degrees of freedom confirm both predictions without adjustable parameters. Requiring neither tangent-space evolution nor prior specification of an order parameter for its computation, trajectory arclength provides a simple, quantitative link between microscopic Hamiltonian motion and collective thermodynamic criticality.

analysis.relevance_note: Equilibrium-averaged Hamiltonian observables give a possible statistical-dynamics connection, though this is physical criticality rather than an entropy-formalism result.
analysis.tldr: Equilibrium trajectory arclength has a predicted thermodynamic kink and a quantified finite-size correction in the attractive mean-field model.
analysis.problem: Detect a collective phase transition through microscopic Hamiltonian trajectory geometry.
analysis.main_result: The equilibrium-averaged arclength, normalized as a Lagrangian descriptor, has a thermodynamic-limit kink exactly at the attractive Hamiltonian mean-field phase transition. The authors attribute it to spontaneous magnetization and derive a leading \(N^{-1/2}\) finite-size correction with an analytic prefactor. Simulations through \(10^5\) degrees of freedom confirm the predictions without fitted parameters. The prefactor, full limit formula and equilibrium assumptions: Not specified in the abstract.

paper.title: One-shot identification of analytic systems
paper.abstract: We study when the coefficients of a linearly parameterized analytic system can be identified from a single input-solution pair. Given a finite dictionary of analytic operators, each admissible input induces a finite-dimensional linear recovery map from coefficients to observed outputs. Coefficient recovery is possible exactly when this map is injective. We define the degenerate input set as the set of inputs for which injectivity fails and prove a zero-one law: either every admissible input is degenerate, or the degenerate set is negligible in the sense that it is compactly slice-null and has zero measure under every nondegenerate Gaussian measure. We then apply this framework to the recovery of matrices, analytic continuous-time dynamical systems, and differential operators. For several ODE and PDE classes, we further characterize the degenerate sets explicitly and identify deterministic choices of inputs that guarantee recovery.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is analytic-system coefficient identification without a central profile theme.

paper.title: A uniform Picard-rank bound for Calabi Yau threefolds with finitely many flop chambers
paper.abstract: We prove that a smooth projective strict Calabi Yau threefold of sufficiently large Picard number either has infinitely many marked flop chambers or admits a fibration on a smooth flop model.

analysis.relevance_note: The abstract concerns Calabi-Yau birational geometry without a stated dynamical connection to the profile.

paper.title: A Keller--Segel Chemotaxis Model on One-Dimensional Moving Domains
paper.abstract: We study a one-dimensional Keller--Segel system on an interval whose boundary moves according to a prescribed contracting law. The boundary motion makes the problem genuinely nonautonomous and destroys the mass conservation available on fixed domains. A time-dependent change of variables, combined with a time reparametrization, reduces the problem to a semilinear system on a fixed interval with time-independent principal part and nonautonomous transport terms. We prove global well-posedness and regularity of weak solutions, and we show that the contraction of the domain yields a uniform bound on the total mass. For the long-time dynamics, our main tool is a singular Gronwall type inequality with an exponentially damped kernel, for which we provide a self-contained version with explicit decay rate and constants, tailored to our setting; under a small gain condition on the boundary velocities, it yields dissipativity with an explicit exponential decay rate, which cannot be obtained from the classical inequality of Henry. With it we prove the existence of the minimal pullback attractor in the universe of families of bounded sets, on the moving domain and then on the fixed rescaled reference domains. Finally, numerical simulations on contracting domains illustrate the effect of the boundary motion on cell aggregation.

analysis.relevance_note: Pullback attractors and nonautonomous dissipative dynamics give a plausible topological-dynamics connection in a PDE model.
analysis.tldr: A contracting-domain Keller-Segel system has well-posed solutions and, under a small-gain condition, a minimal pullback attractor.
analysis.problem: Analyze long-time dynamics when boundary contraction destroys fixed-domain mass conservation.
analysis.main_result: A time-dependent coordinate change and time reparametrization yield a fixed-interval semilinear problem with nonautonomous transport. The authors prove global weak-solution well-posedness and regularity, and a uniform total-mass bound from contraction. A singular Gronwall inequality with exponentially damped kernel gives explicit-rate dissipativity under a small-gain condition on boundary velocities, leading to a minimal pullback attractor in the universe of bounded-set families on moving and rescaled domains. Numerical simulations illustrate aggregation. The small-gain inequality and decay constants: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Time-dependent coordinate transformation and time reparametrization

analysis.context: Nonautonomous dissipative dynamics on moving domains.

paper.title: Aggregation Rules Induced by KL-Regularised Preference Dynamics on Networks
paper.abstract: We study agents that each align a model to their own preference data while observing one another, and ask which aggregation rule the resulting policies implement. Each round, an agent takes one KL-regularised step. The step involves a reference that the agent is penalised for leaving and a challenger against which its responses are compared, and each of the two may be the agent's own or an average over the agents it observes; attention need not be reciprocal. Aggregating the reference makes the rule collective. Agent $v$ then has the weight $\pi_v/\beta_v$, its share of the network's long-run attention divided by its temperature. If, in addition, the challenger is fixed, the agents concentrate on the response maximising $\sum_v(\pi_v/\beta_v)r_v(y)$, where $r_v$ is agent $v$'s reward, and the rule is cardinal. If the reference is fixed and the challenger aggregated, the agents' policies at a fixed point generally differ, and any weighted mean of them is an approximate maximal lottery whatever the weights, so the dynamics select no weighting. If both are aggregated, the rule is ordinal: averaged over rounds, the collective policy is a maximal lottery of the influence-weighted preference kernel, up to a slack that we bound. Where a collective rule exists, its weights depend only on the attention weights and the temperatures.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is network preference aggregation and model alignment without a central dynamical-systems profile theme.

paper.title: Connected Lie groups with a left-invariant intrinsic chronometer
paper.abstract: In this paper, we investigate left-invariant intrinsic chronometers (time functions) on connected finite-dimensional Lie groups. We formulate and prove sub-Lorentzian analogs of V.\,N.\,Berestovskii's classical direct and inverse theorems. A one-to-one correspondence is established between chronometers satisfying the proposed system of axioms (including upper semi-continuity and the condition that the interiors of chronological rhombi form a base for the topology) and smooth left-invariant sub-Lorentzian structures. It is shown that an axiomatic chronometer uniquely determines a closed, pointed, convex cone in the Lie algebra, whose linear span satisfies the Chow--Rashevskii condition, and an upper semi-continuous concave positively homogeneous anti-norm on it. Conversely, it is proved that any such algebraic structure satisfying a local chronologicity condition induces an intrinsic chronometer with the required properties. The proofs rely on local estimates in exponential coordinates, the Hahn--Banach separation theorem, and properties of weak limits in optimal control problems.

analysis.relevance_note: Left-invariant group geometry and topology provide a possible group-dynamics connection, although the abstract concerns chronometric structures.
analysis.tldr: Axiomatic intrinsic chronometers correspond exactly to the stated smooth left-invariant sub-Lorentzian structures.
analysis.problem: Characterize intrinsic time functions on connected finite-dimensional Lie groups.
analysis.main_result: The author proves sub-Lorentzian direct and inverse analogues of Berestovskii theorems. Chronometers satisfying the axioms, including upper semicontinuity and chronological-rhombus interiors forming a topology base, correspond one-to-one to smooth left-invariant sub-Lorentzian structures. Each determines a closed pointed convex Lie-algebra cone with Chow-Rashevskii spanning condition and an upper-semicontinuous concave positively homogeneous anti-norm; every such pair determines a chronometer. The remaining axioms and constructive formulas: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Left-invariant Lie-group geometry and intrinsic chronological topology.

paper.title: Holomorphic Foliations with a Single Singularity on Orbifold Projective Surfaces
paper.abstract: We investigate holomorphic foliations on orbifold projective surfaces with cyclic divisor class group, assuming that the foliation has a unique singular point of algebraic multiplicity one. If the normal degree of the foliation is sufficiently large, then we prove that it admits no invariant algebraic curve. Furthermore, we present several examples showing that the bound obtained is optimal.

analysis.relevance_note: Invariant-curve exclusion and holomorphic foliation classification give a related complex-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: Degree-two projective-plane foliations with the stated singularity restriction are classified, with three families lacking algebraic invariant curves.
analysis.problem: Classify degree-two projective foliations having only saddle-node and nilpotent singularities.
analysis.main_result: The authors classify all degree-two foliations on \(\mathbb P^2_{\mathbb C}\) whose singularities are only saddle-nodes or nilpotent points, up to projective equivalence. The method uses the Campillo-Olivares bijection with polar configurations. Three resulting families have no algebraic invariant curve. The family equations and additional classification details: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Projective holomorphic foliations and invariant algebraic curves.

paper.title: On the space of left orders on the groups $QI(\mathbb{R}_+),\,QI(\mathbb{R}_+)/H \text{ and }G_\infty$
paper.abstract: We introduce the notion of a left order on a group with a certain specification of signs for the elements of a subset. We obtain an equivalent criterion for the existence of such a left order and apply it to obtain a new proof of the fact that any of the groups $QI(\mathbb{R}_+),\,QI(\mathbb{R}_+)/H,\,G_\infty$ admits infinitely many non-Conradian left orders. We introduce the notion of separation of free subsemigroups of a left ordered group by its left translation induced actions on a point in the group and show that the above three groups admit such left orders. We also construct a subset of the set of left orders on any of the three groups, show the subset is a perfect set and give a new proof of the fact that the sets of the left orders on these three groups are uncountable.

analysis.relevance_note: Left-translation actions, ordered groups and perfect spaces of orders directly match group actions and topology.
analysis.tldr: The three stated groups admit separating non-Conradian orders and perfect subsets of their order spaces, giving uncountability.
analysis.problem: Understand prescribed-sign left orders and separation of free subsemigroups by translation actions.
analysis.main_result: For \(QI(\mathbb R_+)\), \(QI(\mathbb R_+)/H\) and \(G_\infty\), the author gives new proofs of infinitely many non-Conradian left orders using a prescribed-sign existence criterion. The groups admit orders separating free subsemigroups through left-translation-induced actions. For each, a constructed perfect subset of the order space yields uncountability. The definitions of \(H\), \(G_\infty\), the criterion and separation conditions: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Ordered groups, translation actions and topology of spaces of orders.

paper.title: Analytical solution of general interface problems for reaction-advection-diffusion equations
paper.abstract: We obtain novel integral representations, expressed as contour integrals in the complex Fourier plane, for the solution of fully nonhomogeneous interface problems for classical reaction-advection-diffusion (RAD) equations with arbitrary initial data on the line and general interface conditions at the origin. Such problems of applied mathematics emerge in a spectacular variety of physical phenomena in mathematical physics, chemistry, continuum mechanics, biology, pharmacokinetics, as well as mathematical finance. A suitable implementation of Fokas' unified transform method is in force herein, with particular challenges arising due to inclusion in the model of lower-order terms, and the generality of interface problems under consideration. To our knowledge, this careful analysis has not appeared in (nor does it follow easily from) literature published so far. Our explicit formulae directly lend themselves to explorations of solutions' qualitative properties such as regularity, asymptotic behavior and well-posedness. This work has also been of utility in the investigation of nonlinear counterparts as well as in the study of phase-transition phenomena, moving-interface and diffuse-interface problems. Such results for RAD and high-order PDEs will soon appear in a series of separate papers.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is explicit interface-PDE solution formulas without a central profile theme.

paper.title: The complete dynamics description of positively curved metrics in the Wallach flag manifold $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$
paper.abstract: The family of invariant Riemannian manifolds in the Wallach flag manifold $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$ is described by three parameters $(x,y,z)$ of positive real numbers. By restricting such a family of metrics in the \emph{tetrahedron} $\cal{T}:= x+y+z = 1$, in this paper, we describe all regions $\cal R \subset \cal T$ admitting metrics with curvature properties varying from positive sectional curvature to positive scalar curvature, including positive intermediate curvature notion's. We study the dynamics of such regions under the \emph{projected Ricci flow} in the plane $(x,y)$, concluding sign curvature maintenance and escaping. In addition, we obtain some results for positive intermediate Ricci curvature for a path of metrics on fiber bundles over $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$, further studying its evolution under the Ricci flow on the base.

analysis.tldr: Projected Ricci-flow dynamics describe curvature-sign preservation and escape for regions of invariant Wallach metrics.

paper.title: Solvable Structures for Hamiltonian Systems
paper.abstract: We develop a geometric framework connecting solvable structures and integrable Hamiltonian systems. For a completely integrable Hamiltonian system with $n$ degrees of freedom, we construct a solvable structure consisting of $2n$ Hamiltonian vector fields that allows us to integrate Hamilton's equations by quadratures. Explicit expressions are derived for the associated Pfaffian forms whose integration yields both the solutions of Hamilton's equations and action-angle variables. This provides a novel interpretation of the Arnold-Liouville theorem in the context of solvable structures. We illustrate the theory by deriving explicit solutions and canonical variables of action-angle type for the open Toda lattice and the rational Calogero-Moser system.

analysis.tldr: Solvable structures of Hamiltonian vector fields integrate the stated completely integrable systems by quadratures and recover action-angle variables.

paper.title: Infinite polynomial patterns in large subsets of the rational numbers
paper.abstract: Inspired by a question of Kra, Moreira, Richter, and Robertson, we prove two new results about infinite polynomial configurations in large subsets of the rational numbers. First, given a finite coloring of $\mathbb{Q}$, we show that there exists an infinite set $B = \{b_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \subseteq \mathbb{Q}$ such that $$\{b_i, b_i^2 + b_j : i < j\}$$ is monochromatic. Second, we prove that every subset of positive density in the rational numbers contains a translate of such an infinite configuration. The corresponding results in the integers are both known to be false, so our results provide natural and relatively simple examples of combinatorial structures that distinguish between the Ramsey-theoretic properties of the rational numbers and the integers. The proofs of our main results build upon methods developed in a series of papers by Kra, Moreira, Richter, and Robertson to translate from combinatorics into dynamics, where the core of the argument reduces to understanding the behavior of certain polynomial ergodic averages. The new dynamical tools required for this analysis are a Wiener--Wintner theorem for polynomially-twisted ergodic averages in $\mathbb{Q}$-systems and a structure theorem for Abramov $\mathbb{Q}$-systems.

analysis.tldr: Finite colorings and positive-density rational sets contain the stated infinite polynomial configurations, via new rational-system ergodic tools.

A combinatorics-to-dynamics translation reduces the proofs to polynomial ergodic averages. paper.title: Beta representations with minimal mean digit
paper.abstract: We consider the problem of minimising the mean digit in beta representations with unrestricted digits, equivalent to a one dimensional affine switched system obtained from a formal limit of a stabilisable two dimensional linear system. We give a countable set of $\beta$ for which the result is given by the usual (greedy) beta expansion, an interval of values for which it is strictly less, a numerical upper bound, and a conditional lower bound for all $\beta$.

analysis.tldr: Minimal mean digits agree with greedy expansions at the stated countable base set, but are strictly smaller on another base interval.

paper.title: Deep Learning of Solver-Aware Turbulence Closures from Nudged LES Dynamics
paper.abstract: The differentiable physics paradigm may be leveraged as an a-posteriori approach for discovering turbulence closure models by embedding a neural network parameterization directly inside the solver and optimizing it given potentially sparse target data. This addresses a key limitation of a-priori learning where direct numerical simulation (DNS) data is used to approximate the subgrid stress with the assumption of a low-pass filter. Closures trained in this a-priori manner frequently lead to unstable deployments due to the mismatch between the assumed filter and the effect of numerical discretizations and coarse-graining. In comparison, while typically stable during deployment, a-posteriori learning incurs high computational costs due to the need to backpropagate through a large eddy simulation (LES) solver. Furthermore, a-posteriori methods are challenging to apply broadly since they require significant modification of existing solvers. Finally, both approaches are limited when generalization is desired across different numerical schemes with their implicit filtering characteristics. In this work, we present a deep-learning approach for turbulence closure modeling built on the continuous data assimilation framework. Our approach enables the a-priori training of closures using DNS data observed only at coarse-grid points without modifying or differentiating through the LES solver, while preserving stability during deployment for the recovery of long-term statistics. We focus on the model's ability to adapt to different discretizations by explicitly conditioning it on the numerical scheme. We use two- and three-dimensional canonical cases to test our framework and show that the learned correction systematically tracks the discretization error of the coarse solver.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is learned turbulence closures and solver discretization without a central profile theme.

paper.title: Learning Forced Multibody Dynamics on Lie Groups
paper.abstract: We introduce an architecture for learning the dynamics of forced mechanical systems evolving on Lie groups, based on discrete forced Euler-Lagrange equations. The proposed method, termed Lie Group Discrete Forced Euler-Lagrange Neural Network (LieDFLNN), learns mechanical dynamics directly from discrete configuration observations, without requiring velocity measurements. This formulation allows the simultaneous identification of unknown mechanical properties and forcing terms, while ensuring that the predicted configurations remain on the underlying Lie group. We develop explicit formulations for rigid body dynamics on $SO(3)$ and $SE(3)$, extend the framework to interacting multibody systems, and introduce a method for learning unknown control forces when the Lagrangian is known. Finally, we evaluate the method through numerical experiments involving rigid body dynamics, nonlinear external forces, controlled systems, and real-world human motion capture data. The numerical results confirm the advantages of incorporating Lie group geometry and discrete variational structure into data-driven modeling of forced mechanical systems.

analysis.tldr: A discrete forced Euler-Lagrange network learns mechanical systems from configurations while preserving the Lie-group configuration space.

analysis.main_result: The LieDFLNN architecture uses discrete forced Euler-Lagrange equations and configuration observations to identify mechanical properties and forcing while keeping predicted configurations on the Lie group. Explicit \(SO(3)\) and \(SE(3)\) rigid-body versions extend to multibody interactions, and a known Lagrangian permits learning unknown control forces. Numerical tests include nonlinear forces, controls and human motion data. The results are numerical evaluations; rigorous approximation or generalization bounds: Not specified in the abstract.
